research_rationale:
Executive Order 13570 of 2011-04-18 (76 FR 22291, PDF pages 1-2) is held as the Federal Register original (govinfo PDF text layer, grade official original). I read it in full and confirm its identity and its clause inventory of 13 scopes as prepared (a dup2 suffix distinguishes repeated item labels in different subsections). Its authority is IEEPA, the NEA and the other statutes it names, and it rests on the national emergency declared in Executive Order 13466 of June 26, 2008, and expanded in Executive Order 13551, on which Executive Order 13570 states it relies. Notice of June 22, 2026 (91 FR 38231; FR Doc. 2026-12836) states that the emergency must continue in effect beyond June 26, 2026, so the emergency, and the order that depends on it, were in effect on the cutoff of 2026-10-14 (NEA section 202(d)). Earlier annual continuation notices for the same emergency are also held; the latest one is relied on because it speaks as of its date. The held original has no own-terms end, expiry or sunset. I read the coverage notes of current-law:usc (U.S. Code release point through 2026-10-09), current-law:ecfr (as of 2026-10-14) and later-events:ofr_catalog (checked 2026-11-25); they show no revocation, supersession or partial revocation of this order. The Federal Register disposition notes for this order contain cross-reference entries only, naming EO 13466, EO 13551, EO 13687 and annual continuation notices (June 13, 2022; June 20, 2025; June 22, 2026), none of which is stated to revoke or supersede this order. No later instrument amends or revokes any clause. The dossier gaps listed as NOTICE identities absent from the census are annual continuation notices and cross-references, not events that change this order; the current-law pointer gaps concern CFR and Code pointers that this claim does not rely on, because the conclusion rests on the order's own text and the continuation notice. The acting-text lead for Executive Order 14294 (Fighting Overcriminalization in Federal Regulations, May 9, 2025) was checked: a scan of the held corpus found no mention of this order in its text, so no provision targeting this order was located. Later orders EO 13687 and EO 13810 recite this order or the emergency; they are recitals, not amendments or revocations. The import prohibition in section 1 is also reflected in OFAC regulations, which are not needed for the conclusion. Savings: none arises because the order remained in force at the cutoff.
